## blowhorn profile accounts

List, map or unmap a profile's social accounts. An account is a Blowhorn connection on one platform; a profile acts through the accounts mapped to it, one per platform, whoever owns them, so a person may keep several profiles and a brand profile reaches the accounts mapped to it. `--map` replaces the profile's account on that platform; `--unmap` leaves the connection itself intact. Needs store.backend=cloud.

```text
blowhorn profile accounts [OPTIONS] name
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Profile name |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--map` | string |  | Map this connection id to the profile, replacing its account on that platform |
| `--unmap` | string |  | Unmap this connection id from the profile; the connection is left intact |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Pace of the random delays between `blowhorn profile accounts` browser steps: a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile accounts kate --json
blowhorn profile accounts kate --map 3f9c2a1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
blowhorn profile accounts layer5 --unmap 3f9c2a1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile auth

Refresh authentication/session state for one or more platforms.

Supported platforms and authentication mechanisms:

linkedin - Persistent browser session. Automated login via `LI_USERNAME` / `LI_PASSWORD` in profile config.yaml, with fallback to manual browser entry.

x - Persistent browser session. Automated login via `X_USERNAME` / `X_PASSWORD` in profile config.yaml, with fallback to manual browser entry.

reddit - Persistent browser session. Automated login via `RDDT_USERNAME` / `RDDT_PASSWORD` in profile config.yaml, with fallback to manual browser entry.

slack - Hybrid: session credentials (xoxc token + d cookie) captured through the run's browser driver (the extension by default), saved to the profile's Slack credential in the store (never config.yaml), and reused for direct API calls. No Slack app install required. Use `--workspace` &lt;host&gt; to capture a new workspace; omit it to refresh every workspace listed under `slack_workspaces` in that credential. Use `--mode` paste for the legacy OAuth-token flow.

bluesky - No browser. Logs in to Bluesky with a handle and app password -- the same login every post makes -- and stores the pair only when Bluesky accepts it, so a refused credential is never saved. For one named profile in a terminal it asks for both (the stored handle is the default; a blank app password keeps the stored one); `--handle` and `--app-password-stdin` supply them without a prompt. Otherwise the stored pair is logged in with and nothing is written.

Use `--profile` all to refresh every local profile after applying any `--exclude` filters.

With `--headless` the browser still opens, as a background window (Chrome is never run headless); only automated credential login is attempted and the manual browser fallback is skipped.

```text
blowhorn profile auth [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | boolean | `false` | Refresh every platform `blowhorn profile auth` can log in to (linkedin, x, reddit, slack). Supersedes `--platform`: when `--all` is set the platform is ignored, whether you typed it or inherited it from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--workspace` | string |  | Slack only: capture session credentials for this workspace domain (e.g. `mesheryio.slack.com`). Opens a browser window; sign in to Slack, and the xoxc token + d cookie are extracted. If omitted, all workspaces listed under `slack_workspaces` in the profile's Slack credential in the store are refreshed. |
| `--mode` | string |  | Slack only: `session` (default) captures xoxc/d via browser; `paste` prompts for a User OAuth Token (xoxp-…) - requires app install. |
| `--handle` | string |  | Bluesky only, one named profile: the handle to log in as (alice.bsky.social; a leading @ is dropped). Stored with the app password only when Bluesky accepts the login; omit it to use the stored handle |
| `--app-password-stdin` | boolean | `false` | Bluesky only, one named profile: read the app password from the first line of stdin, so it never reaches argv, the daily log or a prompt. A blank line is refused and nothing is written |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Pace of the random delays between `blowhorn profile auth` browser steps: a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile auth --platform x --profile alex
blowhorn profile auth --all --profile alex
blowhorn profile auth --platform slack --profile alex --workspace mesheryio.slack.com
blowhorn profile auth --platform slack --profile alex --mode paste
blowhorn profile auth --platform linkedin --profile all --headless
blowhorn profile auth --platform bluesky --profile alex
printf '%s\n' "$APP_PASSWORD" | blowhorn profile auth --platform bluesky --profile alex --handle alex.bsky.social --app-password-stdin --json
blowhorn profile auth --platform linkedin --profile kate --headed --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile current

Show the active profile after resolving CLI, env, and config defaults.

```text
blowhorn profile current [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn profile current` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile current
blowhorn profile current --config ~/.blowhorn.yaml
```

Output: text.

## blowhorn profile delete

Retire a profile by moving data/profiles/&lt;name&gt; -- config.yaml, data/ and every saved browser session -- to data/profiles/.trash/&lt;name&gt;-&lt;timestamp&gt;. Nothing is ever removed: the browser sessions are the expensive part of a profile and the move keeps them recoverable. The profile's row in the store's profiles is retired first (soft-deleted, so `--profile` all stops reaching it); a profile the store never listed just moves. Needs the store: unreachable is exit 3 and nothing moves. Requires `--yes`; `--dry-run` shows what would move and where.

```text
blowhorn profile delete [OPTIONS] name
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Profile name (the directory under data/profiles/) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes` | boolean | `false` | Confirm the move to data/profiles/.trash/; without it the command refuses and exits 1 |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn profile delete` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile delete sam --dry-run
blowhorn profile delete sam --yes --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile get

Print one profile's settings with every secret masked: its config.yaml, with the GitHub keys (GH_\*) read from its credential in the store. Keys whose names contain PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN or COOKIE are rendered as \{"set": true\} or \{"set": false\}; their values are never printed, in JSON or in the table. A store that cannot be reached leaves the GitHub keys out and is named on a Credentials: line.

```text
blowhorn profile get [OPTIONS] name
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Profile name (the directory under data/profiles/) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn profile get` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile get kate
blowhorn profile get kate --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile set

Write KEY=VALUE pairs safely. GitHub keys (`GH_TOKEN`, `GH_USERNAME`) are stored in the profile's GitHub credential in the store, where runs read them, and never in the file; a blank value clears a key. Every other key goes into data/profiles/&lt;name&gt;/config.yaml: the file is round-tripped with its key order preserved, rewritten atomically under a file lock, and only the README template keys (plus `GH_USERNAME`, slack_workspaces and the &lt;WORKSPACE&gt;_SLACK_\* session keys) are accepted unless `--allow-unknown` is passed. Every refusal comes before anything is written. The output names the keys that changed and never echoes a value. Replacing a credential an API check judges (`GH_TOKEN`, the Bluesky handle or app password, a Slack token or captured session) sets that platform back to not checked in profile status until the next check, because each such check records which credential it judged. A browser platform's check is about its saved session and stays.

`--create` makes a new profile in both halves: it resolves EMAIL to the Blowhorn user the profile is bound to, writes the profile's row in the store's profiles, and only then scaffolds data/profiles/&lt;name&gt;/config.yaml from the template plus data/ and browser/. EMAIL is required. `--create` needs the store: when it cannot be reached the create is refused with exit 3, nothing is written on either side and no directory is scaffolded, because a profile with no row is one no job can select. An email no Blowhorn user holds, or one that several hold, is refused by name; `--subject` &lt;uuid&gt; names the user directly on those two branches, is refused when it names no live user, and is refused when EMAIL resolves to someone else. A profile is never created without a Blowhorn user: there is no `--force`. The same email already bound to another profile, or a name held by another user's profile, is refused rather than renamed.

`--register` adds a profile that exists only under data/profiles/ to the store's profiles: the same resolution and refusals, no scaffold, EMAIL read from config.yaml when not given, and safe to run again.

```text
blowhorn profile set [OPTIONS] name [assignments...]
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Profile name (the directory under data/profiles/) |
| `assignments ...` | no | KEY=VALUE pairs to write (slack_workspaces takes a comma-delimited list) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--create` | boolean | `false` | Create a new profile: resolve EMAIL to its Blowhorn user, write its row in the store's profiles, then scaffold data/profiles/&lt;name&gt;/\{config.yaml,data/,browser/\} from the README template; needs the store, and refuses to touch a profile that already exists |
| `--register` | boolean | `false` | Add a profile that already exists under data/profiles/ to the store's profiles: the same resolution and refusals as `--create`, no scaffold, EMAIL read from config.yaml when not given, safe to run again |
| `--subject` | string |  | The Blowhorn user id (a uuid) the profile is bound to, for an EMAIL no user holds or several hold; refused when it names no live user, or when EMAIL resolves to someone else |
| `--allow-unknown` | boolean | `false` | Accept keys outside the config.yaml template (the template keys, `GH_USERNAME`, slack_workspaces and &lt;WORKSPACE&gt;_SLACK_\* are always accepted) |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn profile set` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile set kate EMAIL=kate@example.com X_USERNAME=katesuttons
blowhorn profile set sam PROFILE=sam EMAIL=sam@example.com --create
blowhorn profile set sam EMAIL=sam@example.com --create --subject 3f2b1c4d-8a9e-4c6b-9d1e-2a3b4c5d6e7f
blowhorn profile set sam --register
blowhorn profile set kate GH_TOKEN=ghp_yourtoken --json
blowhorn profile set alex slack_workspaces=mesheryio.slack.com,acme.slack.com
blowhorn profile set kate CUSTOM_NOTE=migrated --allow-unknown
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile status

Report what each local profile is set up for: the platforms it holds an account for (credential key names only -- values are never printed), the browser session directory and its last-modified time, whether another blowhorn process holds its lock, the last recorded session check, and whether the profile is excluded by default. No browser and no platform network by default: accounts are read from config.yaml, and GitHub's from the store, once for every profile. A store that cannot be reached leaves GitHub unknown and is named on a Credentials: line, not fatal, and a check made then skips GitHub and keeps its last recorded result. With `--json` each platform also carries account_status: the status of the profile's account in your Blowhorn account (connected, disconnected, ...), read once for every profile, or null when none is mapped.

`--check-sessions` runs a read-only probe per configured platform (LinkedIn, X and Reddit open the saved session in a background window and look for the signed-in page; GitHub, Bluesky and Slack call their APIs) and records the result in data/profiles/&lt;name&gt;/data/session_status.json, and records a LinkedIn, X or Reddit sign-in it finds (or one that ended) on the profile's account in your Blowhorn account. It never logs in, never types a credential, and reports `busy` instead of waiting when a session is in use. `--check-platform` runs that same probe for one platform only and leaves every other platform's recorded result alone; `--check-platform` github checks the profile's GitHub token in the store against GitHub (the login it signs in as, its scopes and what they lack) with no browser at all. `--roster` additionally reads the profiles roster from the store to show which platforms each profile has a handle for; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3, and a roster that reads empty or cannot be read is reported on a Roster: line, not fatal. `--chrome` additionally reads this machine's Chrome profile mappings from the store, once, and Chrome's own profile list, and adds a Chrome column: the mapped Chrome profile directory and whether the name and account recorded when it was mapped still match (drift, missing, unknown). A mapping is identity, never permission. A Chrome profile list that cannot be read is reported on a Chrome: line, not fatal.

```text
blowhorn profile status [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check-sessions` | boolean | `false` | Probe each configured platform's saved session read-only (in a background browser window unless `--headed`) and record the result in data/profiles/&lt;name&gt;/data/session_status.json; never logs in, and reports `busy` instead of waiting for a session another blowhorn process is using |
| `--check-platform` | string |  | Run the `--check-sessions` probe for this one platform only (implies `--check-sessions`) and leave the other platforms' recorded results as they are. One of: linkedin, x, reddit, hn, slack, bluesky, github; github, bluesky and slack are API calls and open no browser. Unlike `--platform` it is never read from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform, so a default cannot narrow a check nobody asked to narrow |
| `--roster` | boolean | `false` | Also read the profiles roster from the store and report which platforms each profile has a handle for. Needs the store: a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3; a roster that reads empty or cannot be read is reported on a Roster: line, not fatal |
| `--chrome` | boolean | `false` | Read this machine's Chrome profile mappings from the store and Chrome's profile list, and add a Chrome column: the mapped directory and whether its recorded name and account still match. Opens no browser; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3 |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn profile`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Pace of the random delays between `blowhorn profile status` browser steps: a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn profile status
blowhorn profile status --json
blowhorn profile status --profile kate,rian --check-sessions --headless
blowhorn profile status --profile all --check-sessions --roster --json
blowhorn profile status --profile kate --check-platform github --json
blowhorn profile status --chrome
blowhorn profile status --check-sessions --dry-run
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn profile switch

```text

```

Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
